rows.title: Collector's Shelf
rows.blurb: Sits on the shelf in your fandom's colours, flares when a script spots a restock or a drop, and keeps the tally of every grail you've landed.
rows.for: Collectors and fandom-deep fans who want a shelf object that wears their colours at rest and looks up the moment something worth knowing happens.
assumes: an external script that can POST to the button's REST reflex endpoint

rows.title: Festival Wristband
rows.blurb: A press cycles the crowd moments you actually want at a show, a light show plays your own sequence for the encore, and a tally keeps count of every event you've brought it to.
rows.for: Concert, festival and con-goers who want a light-up keepsake that is actually theirs - configured once, and ready again at the next show.

rows.title: Game Night Rig
rows.blurb: A push-to-talk toggle you can feel without looking, three macro presses beside your mouse hand, and a light that says whether your mic is live.
rows.for: PC gamers who want a physical key outside the keyboard, and a light that means something without alt-tabbing to check.
assumes: a voice-chat or conferencing app with a global mute hotkey

rows.title: Home Studio
rows.blurb: Arms record, drops a marker and taps tempo without leaving the take - the light doubles as your DAW's transport state.
rows.for: Solo producers and songwriters working in a DAW most evenings.

rows.title: Matchday
rows.blurb: Idles in your team's colours, steps through the stages of the game with a press, and tallies every scoring play.
rows.for: Season-ticket holders and watch-party hosts who want their team's colours on the desk and an easy way to mark the big moments without checking a score app.
assumes: an external script that can POST to the button's REST reflex endpoint

rows.title: On a Call
rows.blurb: One press mutes your call and flips the light to busy; ten minutes before your calendar's next meeting, it goes red on its own.
rows.for: Remote and hybrid workers whose desk sits by a door people walk through, who want the do-not-disturb light to know about a meeting before they do.
assumes: a voice-chat or conferencing app with a global mute hotkey
a calendar that publishes a secret .ics link (Google/Outlook/iCloud "secret address in iCal format")

rows.title: Smart Home Panel
rows.blurb: A control surface fires the automations you already built over webhook, and the light mirrors whatever your setup already knows - a door open, the laundry done, someone home.
rows.for: Home Assistant and MQTT tinkerers who want one physical control wired into automations they already have, not a phone app nobody else in the house opens.
assumes: an external script that can POST to the button's REST reflex endpoint

rows.title: Stage Cues
rows.blurb: One press panics the backing track to silence, a second opens patch-and-transport control wired to your rig over MIDI, and a tally counts the sets you've played.
rows.for: Gigging musicians running backing tracks and patch changes who need one hand-reachable control that works without a glance.

rows.title: Streamer's Deck
rows.blurb: The LED is your on-air light and it is on camera - one press flips the scene, one mutes the mic, one starts the clip.
rows.for: Twitch/YouTube/TikTok streamers running OBS at a busy desk.
assumes: OBS Studio with matching global hotkeys (Settings > Hotkeys)
a voice-chat or conferencing app with a global mute hotkey

rows.title: The Desk Default
rows.blurb: One button, four things: a focus timer, a mute key, a do-not-disturb light, and a shortcut - the honest all-purpose scene for anyone at a computer.
rows.for: Anyone with a computer and a desk who wants one object doing the four small things they reach for all day, rather than a niche use.
assumes: a voice-chat or conferencing app with a global mute hotkey

rows.title: The GM's Table
rows.blurb: A press sets the room's mood light, a second app steps through whose turn it is - a table-side prop that does two jobs without a laptop open.
rows.for: Weekly tabletop game masters who want a physical prop at the table, not another screen.

rows.title: Time, Not Numbers
rows.blurb: Start a timer with one press and watch time pass as colour instead of digits - no screen, no nagging, no app to open.
rows.for: People who are time-blind, pay a real cost to task-switch, and want an off-screen way to feel time passing.

rows.title: Tinkerer's Bench
rows.blurb: A stocked reference config, not a demo - one of every look shape, a reflex listening for a webhook, and a control surface wired to a generic script hook, all ready to rename.
rows.for: Makers who read the schematic before the manual and want to see the whole vocabulary in one file before they start editing it.
assumes: an external script that can POST to the button's REST reflex endpoint
